test.name: Analyze the identity conflict (c_002)
test.description: An identity conflict asks whether the Patrick Flynn in one record is the same person as the Patrick Flynn in another. Different analytical shape from fact conflicts — one competing assertion rather than multiple, and the question is identity rather than which value is correct.

input.delegation:
Analyze identity conflict c_002 and either resolve it or flag what additional evidence would be needed.

conflictId: c_002
projectPath: <workspace>

judge_context: Should treat c_002 as an identity question (is record A's subject the same person as record B's subject) rather than as a fact disagreement
Should note that an identity conflict can have only 1 competing_assertion_id — the assertion whose person-link is uncertain — unlike fact conflicts which need ≥2

Should resolve c_002 and write what makes the resolution stand: the 1850 and 1860 household placement, and the certificate's father name as a second informant's agreement. Residual doubt about household 197 belongs in the resolution rationale, not in a deferral.

Outcome: c_002 ends resolved with preferred_assertion_id a_001. Ruling (senior genealogist, #4326): c_002 resolves, preferred_assertion_id a_001. Patrick is in Thomas Flynn's household in 1850 (age 5) and 1860 (age 15), and the 1908 certificate names Thomas Flynn as father through a different informant (the son-in-law). Those agree. The rival Patrick in household 197 appears only in the conflict's description, with no record of his own, so nothing on file supports him. An analysis that calls the father's name circular and defers is the wrong outcome.
